ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Repolarization vulnerability

A 64-year-old woman receiving chemotherapy has persistent vomiting, potassium 2.8 mmol/L and magnesium 1.2 mg/dL. Ondansetron is considered while she is receiving another QT-prolonging medication. Which complication is most directly promoted by this combination?

  1. Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia
  2. Atrial septal rupture
  3. Digoxin-mediated bidirectional ventricular tachycardia
  4. Acute aortic dissection
  5. Torsades de pointes
Answer and explanation

Torsades de pointes

Electrolyte depletion and QT-prolonging drugs compound delayed ventricular repolarization and torsades risk.

Option explanations

Torsades de pointes: Electrolyte depletion and QT-prolonging drugs compound delayed ventricular repolarization and torsades risk.

Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia: AV nodal reentry is not the characteristic QT-related arrhythmia.

Atrial septal rupture: A structural septal defect is not produced by QT prolongation.

Digoxin-mediated bidirectional ventricular tachycardia: No digoxin exposure is described.

Acute aortic dissection: Aortic dissection is unrelated to this repolarization effect.
